newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Bezeq opposes IPO by Pelephone unit.
newsitem.headline: Bezeq opposes IPO by Pelephone unit.

text.p: Bezeq Israel Telecom and Motorola Israel strongly oppose an effort by their joint venture Pelephone cellular telephone subsidiary to go public, a Bezeq source said on Sunday.
"The company is very, very much against a Pelephone offering before Bezeq. It's very, very profitable and there's no need to take out equity," the source told Reuters.
The source said Pelephone, Israel's largest cellular telephone company, had hired two investment banks to prepare valuations without the knowledge of Bezeq's board.

Bezeq and Motorola had since turned to the Communications Ministry to complain, but the ministry had not yet responded. The source said an initial public offering in Pelephone would not be likely if the managements of the two controlling shareholders opposed it.
"We don't want it to affect the Bezeq offering....It would cause a distraction," said the source.
Ayala Bar, spokeswoman for the Communications Ministry, confirmed that the idea of floating Pelephone had been discussed but offered no further details.

Bezeq, 76 percent owned by the Israeli government, has been planning to make a global offering for some time. The offering has been delayed while the government seeks to reach an agreement with Britain's Cable and Wireless Plc over its future status in Bezeq.
Cable & Wireless bought up about 10 percent of Bezeq in the Israeli stock market in the spring of 1995 and has since expressed an interest in increasing its stake. The government is opposed.
The Bezeq source said the government would have to offer something to Cable & Wireless in exchange for a standstill agreement.

Bar said the government and Cable & Wireless had discussed the possibility of forming an equally owned joint venture company that would hold 20 percent of Bezeq. The source said this would enable C&W to report its Bezeq holding on an equity basis, which its 10 percent holding does not allow under British accounting rules.
Bar stressed that the joint venture was one of several ideas raised. She said both sides saw it as a priority to reach an agreement and hoped to reach one soon.
